Results Figures & Statistics (v2 — Revised)¶

Dissertation: Examining the effects of theta-tACS over left DLPFC on reward-based learning across the adult lifespan

This notebook produces all manuscript figures and statistical tests, organized to mirror the Results section. Key revisions in v2:

  • Reduced cognitive composite (5 universally-available measures) as primary; original composite as sensitivity
  • Consistent median age split throughout all subgroup analyses
  • Boundary-hit audit for RW learning rate estimates
  • EEG reference robustness check for θ_p95 findings
  • Cognitive composite reliability and missingness documented

Results Structure¶

  1. §3.1 Blinding Integrity
  2. §3.2 Baseline Behavioral Characterization
  3. §3.3 H1.1: Cognitive Function and Baseline Learning (Preregistered)
  4. §3.3.1 H1.1 Exploratory: Age × Cognition Interactions
  5. §3.4 H1.2: Reward/Punishment Sensitivity (Preregistered)
  6. §3.5 H2.1: Stimulation Effects (Preregistered)
  7. §3.6 H2.2: Age Moderation of Stimulation (Preregistered)
  8. §3.6.1 H2.2 Exploratory: Subgroup Decomposition
  9. §3.7 Physiological Measures
  10. §3.8 Survey Measures & Individual Differences
  11. Supplementary Analyses
  12. Export

1. Blinding Integrity (§3.1)¶

======================================================================
Blinding Integrity Analysis
======================================================================

Data: 141 run-level observations from 38 participants

--- Contingency Table ---
                 Participant Guess
Actual Condition   Active    Sham    Total
---------------------------------------------
     Active            48       23       71
      Sham             39       31       70
---------------------------------------------
     Total             87       54      141

--- Signal Detection Metrics ---
  Hits (say Active | Active):            48 / 71 = 67.6%
  Misses (say Sham | Active):            23 / 71 = 32.4%
  False Alarms (say Active | Sham):      39 / 70 = 55.7%
  Correct Rejections (say Sham | Sham):  31 / 70 = 44.3%

  d' (sensitivity):  +0.31  (near zero — no discrimination)
  c (criterion):     -0.30  (no strong bias)

  Overall accuracy: 56.0% (79/141)
  Binomial vs 50%: p = 0.178
  χ² = 1.64, p = 0.201

--- By Counterbalance Order ---
Order    N_runs        Hits          FA       d'      Acc
------------------------------------------------------------
A             59       69.0%       56.7%   +0.31    55.9%
B             82       66.7%       55.0%   +0.30    56.1%

======================================================================
Summary
======================================================================

✓ Blinding appears INTACT:
  • Accuracy (56.0%) not significantly different from chance
  • d' (0.31) indicates minimal discrimination ability
  • No significant association between actual condition and guess

3. H1.1: Cognitive Function and Baseline Learning (§3.3)¶

Preregistered: OLS regression, WSLS DVs ~ global cognition + age + education.
Revision: Uses REDUCED composite as primary; original composite as sensitivity check.

  N = 35

Strategic vs. perseverative interpretation:
Younger subgroup (below J-N threshold, age < 29)
======================================================================

N = 14 (age < 29)

1. Lose-shifting × accuracy:
   r = -0.233, p = 0.423
   → Less lose-shifting associated with HIGHER accuracy (consistent with strategic staying)

2. Lose-shifting × win rate:
   r = -0.334, p = 0.243

3. Cognition × accuracy (zero-order):
   r = +0.095, p = 0.748

4. Cognition × accuracy, controlling for p(shift|lose) (partial r):
   r = -0.057, p = 0.847

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Interpretation:
  Less lose-shifting is directionally associated with higher accuracy
  (r = -0.233), consistent with strategic probability-matching.
  Partial r between cognition and accuracy controlling for lose-shifting
  is near zero (-0.057), suggesting cognition's influence on
  performance in young adults operates primarily through the lose-shift pathway.

  Note: N = 14; these within-subgroup associations should be
  interpreted cautiously given the small sample.

==========================================================================================
SUMMARY & RECOMMENDATIONS
==========================================================================================

1. PROBLEM: Digit Span, BVMT, and Trails A are available ONLY for 40+ participants.
   The current composite uses different measures for younger vs older adults.
 
2. SOLUTION: Build a reduced composite from 5 universally-available measures:
   - Attention: Flanker + Running Dots (97-100% coverage)
   - Memory: HVLT (100% coverage)  
   - Speed: Salthouse Letter + Salthouse Pattern (100% coverage)
 
3. REPORTING STRATEGY:
   a. Report the reduced composite as primary (homogeneous across age)
   b. Report original composite as sensitivity check
   c. Transparently document the missingness pattern
   d. SCD-Q as supplementary self-report measure
 
4. FOR THE MANUSCRIPT:
   - §2.6.1: Describe both composites, missingness table, reliability
   - §3.3.1: Report Age × Cognition interactions with both composites
   - §4.2: Discuss implications of composite composition
   - Deviations subsection: Note the missingness pattern
